messages:
sam: FYI the nightly perf CI flagged a 95th-pct latency regression on small-batch (batch_size=4) for model-x v2. Bench ID 4092. Link: https://ci.internal/bench/4092
perf-bot: alert: perf-ci: regression detected — 95th 120ms -> 360ms. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/bench/4092
anya: grabbing logs now. @liam can you pop the profiler on the nightly shard that ran this? looks like scheduler noise?
liam: on it. which runner? runner-3 or runner-7?
sam: runner-7. failure window ~ 02:12-02:30 UTC. trace id: 0x7f2c
marisol: quick note — I saw a similar blip last week when redis cache warmed. Can we rule out cache eviction?
anya: good call. I pulled redis metrics — eviction spikes at 02:09, but keys warmed by 02:15. attaching snippet:
```text
redis_evictions: 02:05: 0, 02:09: 243, 02:12: 0
cache_hit_rate: 98% -> 76% at 02:10 -> recovers
```
liam: starting perf profiler (flame) on runner-7. command:
```bash
ssh runner-7
sudo perf record -g -o /tmp/bench4092.perf -- ./run_bench --id 4092
```
sam: if profiler heavy — can we run with sampling 99Hz vs default? @liam set sampling=99
liam: set and running. ETA ~6m. will post flame link.
perf-bot: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/perf/4092/logs.tar.gz, s3://redwood-ci/perf/4092/perf.data
marisol: also check GPU SM utilization — past regressions were kernel scheduler thrash when SM % dropped under 20% for short windows.
anya: good point. I pulled GPU stats: utilization fell to 12% at 02:13 for ~30s. attaching:
```text
gpu0: util 87% -> 12% @02:13 -> 89% by 02:14
gpu0: mem_clk stable, temp normal
```
liam: flame shows a long wait in cudaMemcpyAsync + small kernel launches; looks like host-side batching stalled. suspect a slow epoll wake from the I/O thread.
sam: ok let's triage root cause: hypothesis order: 1) redis eviction caused cache miss -> host stall 2) kernel scheduler thrash 3) infra noise (OOM killer?). Next steps: @marisol can you check node-level syslogs for 02:10-02:16? @anya please correlate queue latency from frontend to runner-7.
marisol: checking syslog now — one message: "systemd: NetworkManager restarted" at 02:11 on runner-7. doesn't ring a bell but may cause socket disruption.
anya: queue latencies spike matches the window: 02:09-02:13 queue wait ~200ms -> normal. forwarding traces to the thread: https://traces.internal/trace/7f2c
liam: flame link: https://perf.internal/flames/4092-runner7. shows userspace epoll_wait in io-thread.
sam: thanks. provisional root cause: short network restart on runner-7 causing I/O thread stalls and exposing cache miss patterns, inflating 95th. mitigation: add small retry/backoff around socket ops + ensure NetworkManager doesn't restart in baking images. I'll file a follow-up PR after we confirm.
marisol: I'll add node watchdog alert for NetworkManager restarts in pre-prod pool.
perf-bot: note: created ticket RW-PI-1123 for follow-up (owner: sam). ETA next week for fix.
sam: thanks all. if profiler confirms the epoll wake issue, I'll merge a quick retry patch and we can backfill a canary. otherwise marking this thread resolved for now :thumbsup:
